look_here_first: FIELD SANDBUR (Cenchrus spinifex sensu current project card): first find a grass bearing individual round, sharply spiny BUR UNITS spaced on an upright head—not a single naked seed. Each green bur/fascicle consists of enclosing modified BRISTLES around true grass spikelets. The three saved photos now show growth habit, individual spiny units and attached head. Separate C. longispinus with a fully mature detached bur: classic regional key gives ~8–40 bristles (often stout/wide inner bases) for C. spinifex versus ~45–75 thinner bristles for C. longispinus. A 2026 Texas revision reinstates additional members of the spinifex complex, so do not declare exact species from a prickly image, or imply Hays County nativity without separate review.

morphology_keys.genus_structure: Sandbur fascicle is a bur of fused/closely attached enclosing bristles around one or more grass spikelets; the whole bur is not one naked seed. In modern broad Cenchrus, not all species bear sharp solid burs.
best_field_traits: Grass with slender foliage and a short head bearing discrete, separated green-to-straw spiny fascicles. The three existing source photographs show that architecture at whole-plant, bur-macro and branch scale.
Two concentric groups of bristles occur in typical sandbur species: inner bristles may unite into a cupule, with protruding tips; outer bristles often shorter and can point backward.

Regional classic C. spinifex key: 8–40 bristles per complete bur (often 6–10 visibly stout dominant spines plus smaller elements); narrower many-bristled C. longispinus often 45–75; count ALL bristles, not only large spikes.
Published spinifex-group bur length often ~5.5–10.2 mm and wider inner bristle bases ~1–3 mm versus longispinus ~8.3–11.9 mm and inner bases ~0.5–0.9(–1.4) mm; ranges and damaged burs overlap.

New 2026 Texas taxonomy of the spinifex group reinstated C. incertus and other old synonyms. Do NOT auto-identify all field sandburs as C. spinifex; require a complete mature fascicle, original plant, Texas key and ideally a herbarium specimen.
crew_field_check: Identify a REAL GRASS first: culm, blade, sheath, collar and seedhead together.
See separate spiny fascicles attached along a slender head; each burr-like structure surrounds actual grass spikelets.
Photograph complete flowering head, then an UNDAMAGED mature detachable bur with 1-mm ruler, front/side/base views.
Under 10–20× count all bur bristles separately (large stout spines + tiny outer ones), check whether inner bases are broad and united into a cupule; examine actual enclosed spikelet(s).
Compare only as provisional C. spinifex-group versus longispinus, echinatus, incertus or other newly reinstated Texas taxa unless a current key confirms ID.
Do not use a barehanded spiny-bur demonstration; handle detached specimens with gloves and forceps. Do not remove it as an 'invasive' merely because it sticks to clothes.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Rooted field plant with scale and locality; entire bur-bearing head clearly separate from nearby grasses
Mature intact individual fascicle placed against 1-mm rule, side/front/base views and its actual point of attachment
Total bristle count, including shorter outer elements, captured by focus-stacked 10–20× macro
Inner broad bristle bases / cupule compared with measured C. longispinus thin narrow bases, both sourced and identified
Careful forceps-opened fascicle showing number of true grass spikelets, glumes and lower/upper florets
True ligule and hairy sheath/collar on same plant, plus specimen/voucher for 2026 taxonomy key where needed

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. spinifex sensu older regional key bears a spiny detachable fascicle with relatively few, broader-tipped inner bristles (8–40 total), versus longispinus usually 45–75 thin bristles in a hairy bur and narrow inner bases. Both can inhabit disturbed sandy sites. C. echinatus and reinstated C. incertus require a Texas-specific up-to-date mature-bur key, not finger-prick severity or one enlarged spine. Setaria bristles usually subtend spikelets separately without a stout fused hard bur; modern broad Cenchrus also contains soft-bristled species such as buffelgrass. Taxon/basionym concepts changed in Wipff (2026); original source ID kept as provisional.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: What is actually inside a sandbur?
steps: FIRST photo: see real sandy grass, narrow blades, and at least two flowering culms carrying separate green spiny bur units.
SECOND photo: look at a close green fascicle with radiating sharp spines, and several additional fascicles along the axis. The finger is a rough comparison only.
THIRD photo: look at separate spike-like groupings of round burrs amid narrow grass leaves. Orange/cream protrusions may be flowers, not seeds.

PHOTO EVIDENCE CHECK: these three archived species-labelled images show only whole spiny fascicles and field architecture. None shows an opened bur with enclosed spikelet, the basal fusion of its bristles, or a true inner grass ligule. The C. longispinus ruler picture belongs to the DIFFERENT species.
Wear gloves and use forceps to photograph an ACTUAL mature undamaged bur above a mm ruler; count all coarse and fine bristles, not just obvious thorns.
Check broad/fused bases versus longispinus narrow bases, and split one with forceps to find real enclosed spikelet(s). Key to species using current Texas taxonomic revision.
Until proven, use Cenchrus sp. or Cenchrus spinifex group and DO NOT infer native/exotic status from the name.
LOOK-ALIKE panel 4: compare upright C. longispinus head, notice multiple spiny fascicles rather than a naked seed; Russian source is not a Texas voucher.
LOOK-ALIKE panel 5: identify true centimeter ruler ticks and both long sharp plus tiny fine bristles; overlap and perspective mean DO NOT infer precise total bristle count.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Bur is a spiny fascicle surrounding true grass spikelets; apparent spine count and genus-level look do not settle species.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Do not puncture fingers, treat a source-determined record as a Texas voucher, or assert species-level identification without mature bur detail.

diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.look_here_first: FIELD SANDBUR GROUP: find separate spiny FASCICLES attached along a narrow 2–8.5 cm flowering axis, not single exposed seeds. Each intact 5.5–10.2 mm bur may surround 2–4 true spikelets. Count ALL coarse and fine bristles and inspect their fused cupule; the historical 8–40-bristle C. spinifex concept overlaps taxa reinstated in Wipff 2026. DO NOT call an unidentified bur definitively C. spinifex.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.growth_form: Warm-season annual or occasionally short-lived perennial, geniculate/ascending 5–80 cm culms in older GrassBase treatments; fibrous-rooted, sometimes rooting at low nodes. Photograph the SAME rooted plant, true blade–sheath collar, whole head and detached mature bur. Do not infer Hays nativity from a weedy sandbur.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.ligule_collar: Very short true ligule around 0.5–1.5 mm, described as a hair fringe by GrassBase/AusGrass and as a membrane with fine hairs by Go Botany; show membrane/base and hairs in a 10–20× face-and-side image, with 1-mm scale. Leaf margins rough; sheath and collar hairs are NOT automatically the ligule.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.fascicle_spikelets: Old broad C. spinifex treatments: 2–4 dorsally compressed spikelets within each mature 5.5–10.2 mm spiny bur; 8–40 flattened bristles, with broad inner bases partially fused into a cupule. Spikelets about 3.5–5.9 mm, each with a lower sterile and upper fertile floret. Count every bristle and spikelet on multiple intact burs; old ranges are GROUP reference data, not sufficient species-level determination after the 2026 Texas revision.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.glumes: After opening the bur, identify two actual membranous glumes, NOT spines. Lower glume approximately 1–3.3 mm, about one-third to half spikelet length, one-veined; upper glume about 2.8–5 mm, 5–7-veined. Kew's broad GrassBase account gives a narrower lower-glume range (~1–1.3 mm), so retain source-specific variation rather than using one hard cutoff.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.lemmas_awns: Lower sterile lemma about 3–5.9 mm, 5–7-veined and membranous, with reduced sterile palea. Upper fertile lemma about 3.4–5.8 mm, firmer/coriaceous, three-veined, with similarly firm fertile palea. No true long lemma awns in this old concept: sharp BUR BRISTLES are involucre structures, not glume/lemma awns. Do not arrow lemma/glume from an unopened bur.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.local_lookalikes: C. longispinus commonly has 45–75 narrower bristles and a narrower inner bristle base in older keys, but ranges, damaged burs and image perspective overlap. C. incertus, C. albertsonii, C. roseus and C. densiflorus require the NEW 2026 Wipff Texas species key and voucher-level comparison; do not silently synonymize or admit them. C. echinatus also produces hard burs; Setaria bristles subtend exposed spikelets rather than enclosing them in the same rigid fused cupule. Sandbur appearance alone cannot determine nativity or control priority.
last_mile_photo_arrow_gaps: One mature, undamaged attached fascicle and another detached from the SAME verified Texas plant, three views (front/side/base), with 1-mm ruler and source-locality/voucher reference.
At 10–20× focus-stack ALL inner and outer bristles; count and mark each only where resolvable; expose their fused cupule and measure individual inner bristle bases.
Open an actual mature fascicle with forceps and photograph all 2–4 enclosed spikelets at 1-mm scale, then dissect one lower and upper glume with veins visible.
Separate one lower sterile lemma/palea and upper firm fertile lemma/palea at 20×; distinguish actual lemma bodies from outer sharp involucre bristles. No unsupported anatomy arrows.
Photograph the true 0.5–1.5 mm collar ligule with scale and rooted annual/short-lived perennial base on same plant.
Use current Wipff 2026 Texas key and source/voucher comparison with C. longispinus, incertus and other segregates; preserve source photo rights and existing annotations.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.public_ready_criteria: Remain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS and SPECIES-CONCEPT HOLD until a vouchered Texas plant is checked against Wipff 2026, intact burs have complete bristle/cupule counts, enclosed glumes and fertile/sterile florets plus ligule are photographed at measurable scale, per-image public rights are recorded, anatomy arrows are pixel-accurate and public learner QA passes. Preserve original taxonomic/range hold and photo/license metadata. Never equate this older broad species concept with confirmed 2026 segregate.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.evidence_scope: Legacy broad spinifex morphology from GrassBase, Go Botany and USDA IDtools is retained as provisional GROUP reference only. Wipff 2026 recognizes multiple reinstated segregates and requires modern Texas key; this edit makes NO taxonomic determination or native-range change.
